the activation and expansion of tumor‐specific T‐lymphocyte precursor cells in situ can be induced and that the resulting tumor‐specific cytotoxic T cells are recruited into tumor sites and exert their cytotoxic activity there.

the activation of tumor‐reactive T‐cell precursors to cytotoxic T cells can be achieved in situ in a sponge matrix model, and that these activated T cells can be recovered from the sponge and used for adoptive immunotherapy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a model system that allows the activation and recruitment of tumor‐specific T cells in situ.

the activation of tumor‐sensitizing precursor cells in situ, the induction of a highly cytotoxic anti-tumor T-cell response in vivo by using a specific tumor vaccine and a sponge matrix compartment, and the recruitment and activation of circulating tumor-specific T cells in situ.
the development of a new approach to tumor immunotherapy, which involves the activation of specific T lymphocytes in the tumor‐cell‐rich environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the sponge matrix system is a useful model system for studying the recruitment and activation of tumor specific immune T cells in situ.
tumor‐specific precursor T cells can be activated in situ into tumor‐specific cytotoxic T cells in the tumor‐bearing animal.
tumor‐specific T‐cell activation can be induced and maintained in situ by the application of an appropriate sponge matrix and tumor vaccine.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated the activation and recruitment of tumor‐specific T cells in the local tumor‐cell environment.
we have demonstrated the in situ recruitment of tumor‐specific CTL, their functional activation and the generation of a tumor‐specific DTH response in a sponge matrix model system.

the activation of T cells in situ in the sponge matrix model was possible, and that the activated tumor‐specific T cells were cytotoxic and able to recruit circulating lymphocytes to sites where tumor cells were located.

the sponge matrix model provides a useful system for the study of the activation of tumor‐sensitive T cells in situ.
